title: fix(service-settings): Google login saves ON when its credentials come from the server
body:
Fixes #24844

Clause-②: no

## What changes

`auth.google_client_id` and `auth.google_client_secret` in `packages/services/service-settings/src/manifests/auth.manifest.ts` are now `required: false` (they were `required: true`). Nothing else moves: no default, `visible` rule, option, label, help text or translation bundle. The `google_enabled` help already states the conjunction (Google is offered once a client ID and a client secret both come through, saved below or set as `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` / `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` on the server, which win over saved values). It still reads true, so it is unchanged. A code comment above the toggle now says why the two keys are not `required`.

One changeset: `@objectstack/service-settings` patch.

## Why

- `SettingsService.setMany` judges `required` against the STORED value. It reads only `OS_*` env names (`envKeyOf`), so the `GOOGLE_*` pair is invisible to it.
- plugin-auth offers Google when the toggle is on and both credentials are available, saved or from the env pair, with the env pair winning (`applyEnvSocialProviderFallbacks` at boot, the Google block of `bindAuthSettings`). It needs the pair to be available. It never needs it stored.
- So on an env-credential deployment, the declaration refused a save that the runtime would honour. `setMany('auth', { google_enabled: true })` answered `SETTINGS_VALIDATION` with `google_client_id/required` and `google_client_secret/required`. The TOUCH gate judges both, because their `visible` reads `google_enabled`. An admin who switched Google off on the page could not switch it back on there.

Route C (the resolver reports the env pair as the source) needs `settings-service.ts` or a spec-level env-name declaration, and both are outside this card. See the decision record below.

## The offer matrix, before and after

This was measured with a one-off probe (not a repo file). It uses a real `SettingsService`, the real `auth` manifest from `builtinSettingsManifests`, a real `AuthPlugin` booted with that service as `settings`, and `AuthManager.getPublicConfig().socialProviders`. The credential values are fake. **Before** is the base build at `df8bb40a03`. **After** is this branch's build at `6c1589e41c`. "Offered" is the providers the login page lists; the source in brackets is whose client ID the registered provider carries.

| deployment | admin action | before: save | before: offered | after: save | after: offered |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| env pair | none (toggle unset) | n/a | google (env) | n/a | google (env) |
| env pair | save ON | **REFUSED** (`required` x2) | google (env), toggle stays unset | saved | google (env) |
| env pair | save OFF | saved | none | saved | none |
| env pair | save OFF, then ON | ON **REFUSED** | **none (stuck off)** | saved | google (env) |
| stored pair | none | n/a | google (stored) | n/a | google (stored) |
| stored pair | save ON | saved | google (stored) | saved | google (stored) |
| stored pair | save OFF | saved | none | saved | none |
| stored pair | save OFF, then ON | saved | google (stored) | saved | google (stored) |
| env + stored | none | n/a | google (env) | n/a | google (env) |
| env + stored | save ON | saved | google (env) | saved | google (env) |
| env + stored | save OFF | saved | none | saved | none |
| env + stored | save OFF, then ON | saved | google (env) | saved | google (env) |
| no credentials | none | n/a | none | n/a | none |
| no credentials | save ON | **REFUSED** (`required` x2) | none | saved | none |
| no credentials | save OFF | saved | none | saved | none |
| no credentials | save OFF, then ON | ON **REFUSED** | none | saved | none |

Four more rows check what a cleared credential does. Their "before" column comes from an emulated base: this branch's build with `required: true` put back on the two keys in memory, which is the only behavioural difference in `service-settings`. The emulation's 16 shared rows were checked against the real base build's reading above, and they match exactly.

| deployment | admin action | before: save | before: offered | after: save | after: offered |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| stored pair | client ID saved as an empty string | **REFUSED** (`google_client_id/required`) | google (stored) | saved | none |
| stored pair | client ID reset (`null`) | saved | none | saved | none |
| env + stored | client ID saved as an empty string | **REFUSED** | google (env) | saved | google (env) |
| env + stored | client ID reset (`null`) | saved | google (env) | saved | google (env) |

**Reading.** For every stored state, the providers offered are the same before and after. Only the saves that the base refused change. Three states can now be saved:

- the toggle ON on an env deployment, which offers Google, the same as the default;
- the toggle ON with nothing available, which offers no Google, the same as the default;
- a credential stored as an empty string. plugin-auth reads that as unset (`asTrimmedString`). The base already reached the same offered state with a `null` reset, as the rows above show.

Who may sign in, and which providers the login page offers, do not change for any deployment shape.

## Pins

`packages/services/service-settings/src/manifests/auth.manifest.test.ts`, on a real `SettingsService` with the real `auth` manifest:

- **declares neither credential key required.**
- **saves Google ON with both credential fields empty, from unset and after an OFF.** The service's env map carries fake `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` / `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` values. `getNamespace` hands plugin-auth `google_enabled: true` from the `global` source and both credentials from `default`, so plugin-auth falls back to the env pair.
- **control: a stored credential pair still saves and reads back.**

The plugin-auth half, which maps stored or env values to offered providers, is already pinned in `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.test.ts`:

- "enables Google from env credentials when google_enabled is explicit true";
- "enables Google from settings-managed credentials";
- "keeps deployment Google credentials ahead of settings-managed credentials";
- "disables env-backed Google when google_enabled is explicit false".

This PR does not touch plugin-auth.

## Ablation (one-off, no permanent file)

`required: true` was put back on both keys through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`: the anchor hit once, and the blob changed `146f1574445f` to `04ddcdc314d2`. Then `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-settings exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/manifests/auth.manifest.test.ts` ran:

- FAIL "declares neither credential key required": `google_client_id: expected true to be false`.
- FAIL "saves Google ON with both credential fields empty, from unset and after an OFF": the promise rejected with `code: 'SETTINGS_VALIDATION'` and fields `google_client_id/required` and `google_client_secret/required`.
- `Tests 2 failed | 16 passed (18)`. The stored-credential control is among the passes.

The restore ran `git checkout HEAD -- PATH` on the absolute path. Afterwards the blob was `146f1574445f`, equal to the HEAD blob; `git diff HEAD` was 0 bytes; `git status --porcelain` showed 0 lines. The file then ran 18 of 18 green. The test imports the manifest from source, so no rebuild was needed for this ablation.

## Verification (head `6c1589e41c`)

- **Closure:** `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '@objectstack/service-settings^...' --filter '@objectstack/plugin-auth...' build`, exit 0. This adds plugin-auth and service-settings themselves to the dispatch's closure, for the probe. Both were rebuilt at the final head.
- **Tests:** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-settings test` gave `Test Files 54 passed (54)` and `Tests 906 passed (906)`.
- **Typecheck:** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-settings typecheck`, exit 0. `tsc --listFiles` includes `src/manifests/auth.manifest.test.ts`.
- **Gates:** `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 66 commands. 65 exited 0. `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exited 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET): it reads every package's `dist/` and needs a whole-tree build, so it was NOT MEASURED locally; CI's `Lint & Repo Gates` runs it.
- **Reconciliation:** `--ran` printed `✓ dispatch-gates --ran: 66 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 65 run, 1 NOT-MEASURED (1 DERIVED from a recorded exit 3)`.

## Decision record (options A / B / C from the card), on the four axes

- **Real business need.**
  - The writer is the Setup → Authentication form (`PUT /api/settings/auth`, which calls `setMany`). The reader is plugin-auth's `bindAuthSettings`.
  - `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx` documents the env pair as a supported deployment shape.
  - The refusal is measured above, including the stuck-off row.
  - **B** and **C** both serve this need. **A** leaves the stuck-off state. C's extra, showing "set via env" on the page, has no measured pull.
- **Long-term soundness.**
  - **B** makes the declaration say what the runtime needs: a credential that is available, not one that is stored.
  - **C** is also truthful. It teaches the resolver a non-`OS_` env name, which is new resolver surface in the 18.x C8 territory.
  - **A** keeps a declaration that is wrong on a documented deployment shape.
- **Making AI mistakes harder.**
  - **B** removes a constraint that is broader than the runtime's need, and adds no consumer-side tolerance. The manifest stays strict, and the help carries the conjunction.
  - Under **A**, an author who reads `required: true` would conclude that the credentials must be stored. That invites bootstrap code that copies the env secrets into settings.
  - **C** adds a mapping declaration that is one more thing to get wrong.
- **Startup focus.**
  - **B** adds no surface and removes one declared constraint.
  - **C** is a capability expansion with no named pull.
  - **A** costs nothing and fixes nothing.

**Recommendation and route taken: B.**

One forward note, a reading and not measured here: objectstack-ai/objectui#13239 makes the console refuse Save while a visible `required` field is empty. With `required: true` kept, that check would block every Save on the Authentication page of an env-credential deployment while Google is on, which is its default. With `required: false`, the console and the server agree.

## Related

- #24776 is the parent card. Its PR #24842 changed only the help text.
- objectstack-ai/objectui#13239 is the console's required check, which reads the same `required` flag.

## Acceptance notes

- An empty-string credential is reachable through the API only. objectstack-ai/objectui#13145 settled that the console clears a field with `null`, and `null` already saved before this change.
- Saving the toggle ON while nothing is available is accepted. The page cannot show that the server's pair is in force (that would be route C); the `google_enabled` help says it instead.
- The probe's real-base reading used builds at `df8bb40a03`. The final-head reading used builds at `6c1589e41c`, after merging `origin/main` (which brought #24853's OAuth-registration status change in plugin-auth, unrelated to the Google binding).
